radiology_report:
Radiology Division | Maastricht UMC+ | 10 January 2025
Examination: Multiparametric prostate MRI
Clinical context: Re-assessment of established malignancy; PSA 86.0 ng/mL; previous biopsy flagged positive.
Observations: Glandular dimensions total 37.29 mL. T2-weighted sequences isolate a discrete hypointense focus within the right mid-gland peripheral zone, spanning roughly 22 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows intense restriction paired with low ADC signals. Post-contrast dynamics demonstrate prompt, localized hyperenhancement compared to adjacent tissue. Capsular integrity remains intact with no seminal vesicle involvement. Pelvic nodes and bladder show no abnormality.
IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right mid-gland. Prostate volume 37.29 mL yielding a PSA density of 2.306 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.9527162.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. van den Berg (GP)
previous_notes.text: Urology clinic visit scheduled to track disease progression after the initial positive biopsy. A May 2024 serum test recorded 57.4 ng/mL, warranting continued monitoring. Recent escalation to 86.0 ng/mL has triggered another clinical review. The patient continues to report negligible urinary complaints, maintaining an IPSS score of 4/35.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. van den Berg (GP)
previous_notes.text: Screening routines first uncovered an asymptomatic PSA spike of 62.3 ng/mL. Subtle lobe asymmetry detected during rectal palpation led to an ultrasound-guided tissue sampling. Urology consultation was arranged for comprehensive assessment. At that visit, no immediate therapeutic actions were necessary.
